Audio Priority Bar 2.9.0 connects and disconnects Bluetooth speakers and headphones from the panel, and keeps the panel steady while its lists change. Coming from 2.8.0, the update installs in place, and your existing priorities and overrides are kept.

## Bluetooth

- Paired Bluetooth speakers and headphones stay listed at their rank while they are off, dimmed. Click one to connect it and switch to it, or hover it and click **Connect** to connect it and let your priorities decide ([#39](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/39)).
- A Bluetooth device that is connected but not in use shows **Connected**. Hover it and click **Disconnect**, or use its actions menu, to release it ([#39](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/39)).
- Listing paired devices needs no permission. The first connect or disconnect asks for Bluetooth permission.

## Panel

- The panel keeps its top edge still while its lists grow or shrink, so rows no longer slide under the pointer when you show hidden and disconnected devices ([#39](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/39)).
- A disconnected device reads **Last seen 1w ago**, and statuses use the full width of a row until you hover it ([#39](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/39)).

## Fixes

- A Jabra headset's battery appears within seconds of turning the headset on, instead of up to a minute later ([#37](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/37)).
- The hover preview no longer opens for a menu bar icon tucked behind the menu bar's hidden items arrow, or from the top edge of the screen. Settings › Menu Bar can allow Accessibility so the preview checks that the icon itself is under the pointer ([#38](https://github.com/camguillory/Audio-Priority-Bar/pull/38)).

## Install

```bash
brew install --cask camguillory/tap/audio-priority-bar
```

Alternatively, download `AudioPriorityBar.zip` and `AudioPriorityBar.zip.sha256` below into the same folder, verify the archive, and move the app to `/Applications`:

```bash
shasum -a 256 -c AudioPriorityBar.zip.sha256
```

The release is universal for Apple silicon and Intel. It is signed with the project's own certificate, not an Apple Developer ID, and not notarized. If macOS blocks the first launch, open **System Settings > Privacy & Security** and click **Open Anyway**.

Connecting a Bluetooth device from the panel asks for Bluetooth permission, and Accessibility is optional, for the hover preview. Jabra Link monitoring may request Input Monitoring permission. Link 380 is hardware-verified. Link 390 is expected to work through the same capability check but remains unverified on hardware, and monitoring fails open when the link state cannot be read.
